subject: Clarify royalty carve-out and rebilling mapping for marketplace addendum
messages:
From: CloudWave Partnerships <partners@cloudwave.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com, finance@cloudwave.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum — billing mapping / royalty carve-out questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the call earlier. We attached our marketplace termsheet and a quick diagram of how CloudWave currently invoices end customers through the marketplace. Before we move to redlines, a couple of items we want to confirm so internal billing can reconcile gross vs. pass-through flows: 

- Royalty carve-out: our finance team expects any OEM/royalty fees charged to end customers to be excluded from Redwood's usage-based fees and to be remitted separately to CloudWave. Is that something Redwood can accept as a carve-out in the Order Form?
- Rebilling mapping: we need to ensure invoice-level mapping from marketplace invoice to Redwood order so that rebates/credits flow correctly back to CloudWave. Can Redwood commit to providing invoice UUIDs on each invoice or a line-level remittance identifier?
- Audit triggers: what events will trigger a marketplace audit? Our procurement policy requires at least 60 days notice and scope-limited sampling.

Attaching: CloudWave_Marketplace_Termsheet_v1.pdf; rebate_flow_diagram.png

If you prefer, we can take a quick 20-min follow-up to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Rebecca Silva
CloudWave Partnerships
partners@cloudwave.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: Marketplace addendum — billing mapping / royalty carve-out questions

Team — forwarding CloudWave's questions below. Can legal and finance confirm: 1) whether we can accept an explicit royalty carve-out on the Order Form (and what limiting language we should propose), and 2) whether our billing/engine can include an invoice UUID or line-level remittance ID to satisfy their rebilling mapping requirement?

Quick asks: 
- Ben: suggested redline approach for the carve-out and an owner for audit notice language.
- Laura: procurement/compliance concerns about the 60-day notice for audits — can we accommodate a scoped sample vs. full-system audit?
- Marcus: ops question — does Dedicated/Dedicated-reseller instrumentation today capture invoice UUIDs on customer invoices? If not, what effort estimate?

I'll loop in solutions if we need product/ops but want to get legal/finance position first.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: Marketplace addendum — billing mapping / royalty carve-out questions

Sofia / team — dug into this with legal and finance. Attaching a working redline (SIV_CW_addendum_redlines.pdf) with high-level recommendations. Main points: 

1) Royalty carve-out: we can accept an explicit carve-out for third-party royalties but recommend limiting language so Redwood only excludes "statutorily required pass-through taxes and documented third-party royalty/usage fees imposed on the end customer by the marketplace or platform". This keeps it narrow and requires CloudWave to provide evidence.

2) Rebilling mapping: Redwood can provide an invoice-level identifier on outbound invoices (invoice_uuid) and include the marketplace order id on the billing export. However:
  - For line-level remittance IDs (per-customer rebate mapping), that capability requires a small engineering change to the billing export. Estimate: 3–4 weeks of work for the billing exports team (can be prioritized for Dedicated/Marketplace partners).
  - In the interim we can provide a mapping report (daily CSV) that joins our internal invoice_uuid to the CloudWave marketplace order ids — acceptable as a temporary remediation.

3) Audit triggers & notice: Legal prefers limiting audit rights to "material discrepancies" discovered in a reconciliation exercise and a 45-day notice for on-site or full-system audits. For scoped sample audits, we can offer a 30-day notice and a predefined scope (max 2 sample months per 12-month period). That aligns with our ISV partner program.

Attachments: SIV_CW_addendum_redlines.pdf

Action items I recommend we send to CloudWave: 1) proposed redline PDF, 2) ask if their billing system can accept our invoice_uuid mapping field, 3) propose the interim daily CSV mapping while engineering schedules the billing export change.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Channel Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2027 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: Marketplace addendum — billing mapping / royalty carve-out questions

Ben / Sofia — thanks for the summary. A couple procurement/compliance flags I want to call out before we share redlines externally: 

- Evidence standard: if we accept "documented third-party royalty/usage fees", we should require either (a) a marketplace invoice that shows the third-party fee line, or (b) a signed reseller agreement that defines the fee. That will prevent overbroad carve-outs.
- Rebilling timing: we should limit any credit/rebate to a 180-day lookback for adjustments to avoid indefinite liability.
- Audit logistics: agree with scoped sampling but ask CloudWave to cover reasonable third-party audit costs if discrepancies exceed a materiality threshold (suggest 3% of disputed volume).

If CloudWave pushes back on the 180-day lookback, we can offer a one-time extended window tied to their onboarding batch (e.g., first 12 weeks after launch).

I'll add redline comments to Ben's PDF and put procurement-approved language inline.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Procurement, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Silva <partners@cloudwave.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace addendum — billing mapping / royalty carve-out questions

Rebecca — thanks for the term sheet and diagram. Please find attached our proposed addendum redlines (SIV_CW_addendum_redlines.pdf). High level: we are willing to accept a narrow royalty carve-out (see comment #3) provided CloudWave (a) supplies supporting marketplace invoices or reseller agreements and (b) limits credit/rebate exposure to a 180-day lookback (procurement request).

On invoicing: we can include an invoice_uuid field on our invoices and provide a daily mapping CSV that ties Redwood invoice_uuid to CloudWave marketplace_order_id while our billing team implements the line-level remittance id (estimated 3–4 weeks). Can you confirm whether your systems can ingest the invoice_uuid field and whether you can accept the interim daily CSV?

Audit: we propose scoped sample audits with 30 days notice; full-system audits require 45 days and are limited to material discrepancies. If final reconciliation shows >3% discrepancy, CloudWave would cover third-party audit fees for the portion above that threshold.

Next steps: please review the redline PDF and let us know any must-have changes. If helpful, we can set up a 30-minute call mid-next-week to walk through the proposed language and the rebate flow diagram.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: SIV_CW_addendum_redlines.pdf
